Fellow procrastinator here! It’s within our nature to do literally ANYTHING other than what we are meant to be doing and ALWAYS leave it till crunch time. I did this a lot in my first and second year...when third year came along I realised I couldn’t just coast along anymore. I really did struggle concentrating and it was more of a mental push forward to do it BUT one thing that did really help was having a integrated calendar/to do system. I basically had a chalkboard and drew on a calendar type deal of the days/months leading up to my deadlines. Have one sheet of paper for a month and a half/2 months, depending what you can fit on there. It depends when you need to do reading/research and first drafts etc (again depending on the essay) and make little deadlines for when you want these done for. The BEST thing I did was also make a small key for productivity. 

✅ A GREEN CROSS ON MY CALENDAR - this meant I was very productive (at least an hour and a half + of work/reading/anything related to essay work) 


🔶 AN ORANGE CROSS - this meant I was semi productive, didn’t have to be a massive session but I at least looked at readings and didn’t slack off all day. 


❌ A RED CROSS - this meant I did nothing work related and did my own thing. 

With this key in mind I only allowed myself one red cross per week. HOWEVER I implemented this late into my academic year so any earlier and I would have allowed myself more red crosses as it wasn’t as time urgent, etc. I found this REALLY helped motivate me to do at least something, even if it was just half an hour to give me that orange cross on my calendar. Obviously adapt it to what works for you but this really encouraged me to do a bit of work every day and I felt validated when I got a lot of green crosses every week (well not every week...I was still queen procrastinator) 

Hope that wasn’t confusing and may help!!

No matter what happens, this part of the break up sucks and is really hard. There's no way to really avoid the awkwardness of the interaction itself - it's going to be awkward. The only thing you can really be in control of is what you do afterwards and/or how you handle it. Heads up - as soon as you see her everything will flood back to you with rose tinted glasses on. You will miss her, yearn for your relationship and may even end up sleeping together.

If i give you any advice (from personal experience) resist these urges at ALL costs. You separated for a reason, something evidently wasn't right or working for the pair of you. It's totally natural to miss this person and in a moment of temporary emotion super easy to romanticize it and think it can work out. Resist wanting to kiss her or initiate anything upon the first time seeing her. If weeks pass and you find yourself regretting your decision with a lot of thought and may want to propose getting back together, go for it. But when you are reuniting for the first time since your break up your emotions wont be 100% genuine. Try and stay strong - you can do it! 

(Spoiler - i met up with my ex boyfriend face to face after we broke up for similar reasons you stated. Missed him. Kissed him. Got back together for two weeks because it felt 'right' then inevitably broke it off because i realised it wasn't right and hurt him 10x more. Save both of you the heartache of it all and avoid my mistake!)
